claims.subject: aib-doc-casp-center-2026

object.value: Stated purpose of the Protein Structure Prediction Center

claims.statement: The Protein Structure Prediction Center states on its home page, as served on 2026-10-30, that its goal is to help advance the methods of identifying protein structure from sequence and that the Center provides the means of objective testing of these methods through blind prediction.

time.note: The page states no date of its own; the snapshot is the retrieval date.

claims.qualification: A self-description on a mutable page, dated only by retrieval. It is not evidence about how the testing is carried out in any particular CASP round.

evidence.passage: Our goal is to help advance the methods of identifying protein structure from sequence. The Center has been organized to provide the means of objective testing of these methods via the process of blind prediction.

claims.subject: aib-doc-casp-center-2026

object.value: Stated aims of the CASP experiments

claims.statement: The Protein Structure Prediction Center states that the Critical Assessment of protein Structure Prediction (CASP) experiments aim at establishing the current state of the art in protein structure prediction, identifying what progress has been made, and highlighting where future effort may be most productively focused.

time.note: Snapshot at the retrieval date; the page carries no date of its own.

claims.qualification: The organiser's statement of its own aims, not an assessment of whether they are met.

evidence.passage: The Critical Assessment of protein Structure Prediction (CASP) experiments aim at establishing the current state of the art in protein structure prediction, identifying what progress has been made, and highlighting where future effort may be most productively focused.

claims.subject: aib-doc-casp-center-2026

object.value: Seventeen previous CASP experiments, CASP1 in 1994 to CASP17 in 2026

claims.statement: The Protein Structure Prediction Center states, on its home page as served on 2026-10-30, that there have been seventeen previous CASP experiments, that the seventeenth completed in August 2026, and it lists them by year from CASP1 (1994) to CASP17 (2026).

time.note: Snapshot at the retrieval date; the page states the completion of CASP17 as August 2026.

claims.qualification: The organiser's own count and year list on a mutable page. The years are the page's labels for each experiment, not dates of particular assessments or publications.

evidence.locator: home page, paragraph before the list of experiments
evidence.passage: There have been seventeen previous CASP experiments. The seventeenth experiment completed in August 2026.

evidence.note: The list continues in the same form to CASP17 (2026).

claims.subject: aib-doc-casp1-description-2026

object.value: CASP1 held in 1994 with 33 targets and 35 prediction groups

claims.statement: The Prediction Center's CASP1 description page states that this large-scale experiment to assess protein structure prediction methods was held in 1994, that 33 protein prediction targets were obtained in three prediction categories, and that 35 prediction groups took part, submitting over 100 predictions.

time.note: The page is undated and is recorded as a snapshot at the retrieval date; the events it describes are dated 1994 in its own text.

claims.qualification: A retrospective description by the organiser, published on an undated page. The page's own wording calls it "This first large-scale experiment"; that priority wording is the page's, not Selekoa's. Numbers are as stated and were not independently checked.

evidence.passage: This first large-scale experiment to assess protein structure prediction methods was held in 1994.

The same paragraph states that 33 protein prediction targets were obtained in three prediction categories — comparative modelling, fold recognition or threading, and ab initio folding — and that 35 prediction groups took part submitting over 100 predictions.

Dates. Every journal document carries the dates its own expression states, by kind: received, accepted, published online, version of record where it differs (AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold 3 both carry a later version of record) and issue date. Where only a month is stated, the month stands (the CASP assessment papers' issue dates). Where no online publication date is stated, the field stays unknown (Foldit 2010, the 2024 AlphaFold database paper). CASP results are recorded as CASP's own pages and assessors state them; the authors' own reports of their CASP entries are separate records, each marked as the authors' report.

Seven records carry a hazardNote: the two AlphaProteo records beyond the publication fact, RFdiffusion's contribution and negative record, ESM3's contribution and the EvolutionaryScale framework record, and the three Evo and Evo 2 records. From those texts only policy-level, dataset-level and publication-level passages were quoted; design tasks, generated proteins, benchmark detail, prompts and all method detail were excluded. No sequence, protocol or design example appears anywhere in the draft. No author email address was copied, although addresses are printed in several of the retrieved texts.
